audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Tryndamere, Skill, Singed, Singed, Tryndamere, Singed, Singed — and level 6 is scored Tryndamere while every sentence of prose about level 6 says the opposite. spikes[1].text: 'Insanity Potion's stat dump makes you tanky enough to run at Tryndamere and force him to pop Undying Rage on your terms'. whys[4] says the same. Meanwhile levels 2 and 3 are scored Skill/Singed while spikes[0] says 'concede the first two levels entirely' and whys[2] admits 'his DPS still edges the full trade'.
audit.why: Emerald+ 51.50% over 969 games is a near-even lane, and the packet chart reads Tryndamere, Tryndamere, Skill, Skill, Singed, Singed, Skill — which matches both the number and the prose the page already prints. The current chart is internally contradictory in two places at once: it gives Singed the stage his own text concedes, and takes away the stage his own text claims.
audit.corrected: Whole chart moved as one atomic group to the packet read across both layers, with the flipped stages' why lines rewritten to state the real reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3].text asserts 'Undying Rage on a 110-second cooldown'. There is no rank at which Undying Rage is 110 seconds.
audit.why: Riot's value is 120/100/80. The whole late-game spike is an argument built on a cooldown number, so a wrong number breaks the argument: at rank 3 it is 80s, forty seconds shorter than the page implies, which changes how often he can survive your attrition and how long your re-engage window actually is. The other three spikes — levels 1-2, level 6, Rylai's — are the right four moments.
audit.corrected: Real value 120/100/80s written into spikes[3].text and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout (W) appears nowhere in either layer. Riot's text: 'decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.'
audit.why: This is the single most Singed-specific ability in Tryndamere's kit and the page is silent on it. Singed's entire pattern is running away with poison behind him — which means his back is turned by definition. Mocking Shout's slow half is conditional on exactly the thing Singed does all game, from 850 range, on a flat 14s. The AD-reduction half is worthless against an AP Singed, so the page is not merely incomplete, it omits the only part of the ability that matters and keeps none of it. A Singed who does not know this reads his failed disengages as bad luck.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout: 14s, 850 range. Its slow only applies while your back is turned — i.e. every time you kite away. Turn to face him through the goo, or eat the slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says 'anti-heal his crits' in tldr, winCon and dosFull, but never names where Singed's anti-heal comes from. Bloodlust (Q) is the heal — 12s, no cost — and Insanity Potion is what makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: 'Anti-heal' is being used as an item instruction only, when Singed's own ultimate is a Grievous Wounds source. That changes the level-6 fight: drinking before the commit is not just a stat dump, it directly halves the Bloodlust heal that is Tryndamere's only sustain. Naming the mechanism turns a vague build note into a sequencing rule.
audit.corrected: Insanity Potion (100s flat) makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds — it caps Bloodlust (12s) for its whole duration. Drink before the commit, not after.
sources: champ-data/_kits/singed.json (Insanity Potion: 'making his Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds')

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] says 'Use Mega Adhesive to root Tryndamere at the edge of your poison cloud'. Mega Adhesive does not root anything on its own; whys[2] repeats the same shape as 'Mega Adhesive root plus Fling'.
audit.why: Riot's Fling text: 'If the target Singed flings lands in his Mega Adhesive, they are also rooted.' The root is a sequence — goo on the ground first, then Fling into it — and stated as a property of the goo the player will drop W on him and wonder why nothing rooted. Order is the whole trick.
audit.corrected: Goo first, then Fling into it. Landing in the Mega Adhesive is what roots.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carries one ability with no number attached and two generic placeholder lines.
audit.why: Every cooldown in this matchup is knowable: Undying Rage 120/100/80, Spinning Slash 12/11/10/9/8, Mocking Shout flat 14, Bloodlust flat 12. Spinning Slash is the punishable one at rank 1 — 12s of no gap-closer is a full proxy trip.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with the real numbers and the Mocking Shout condition.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a proxy-or-farm fork: if the wave is near his side, walk behind his tower and start absorbing minions under Insanity Potion's cooldown — Tryndamere's kit is built for dueling, not for chasing a Poison Trail into his own jungle while his tower bleeds. Once Insanity Potion is online at 6 the lane flips meaningfully — the armor, MR, and regen make his crit pattern much less punishing, and you can finally run at him in a straight line, drop Mega Adhesive to cut off the Spinning Slash escape route, and force him to burn Undying Rage on a 1-HP kite that still has your cloud burning underneath him. The correct play after he pops R is to disengage entirely: sit just outside auto range, let the 5 seconds tick, then re-engage the moment Undying Rage falls.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a proxy-or-farm fork: if the wave is near his side, walk behind his tower and absorb minions — Tryndamere's kit is built for dueling, not for chasing a Poison Trail into his own jungle while his tower bleeds. Watch Mocking Shout on the way out: it is a flat 14 seconds from 850 range and its slow only applies while your back is turned, which is every second you are kiting. Once Insanity Potion is online at 6 the lane flips — the stats blunt his crit pattern and Poison Trail now applies Grievous Wounds, halving the 12-second Bloodlust he lives on, so you can run at him and force Undying Rage. After he pops it, disengage: sit outside auto range, let the 5 seconds tick, then re-engage.

notes: Mocking Shout was the find here and it was absent from every field: its slow is conditional on the target's back being turned, which is Singed's entire pattern, and it is a flat 14s from 850 range. Also corrected a fabricated cooldown — Undying Rage was written as '110 seconds' and is 120/100/80 — and the Mega-Adhesive-roots claim, which is really Fling-into-the-goo. Level chart moved as one group to the packet read (Trynd, Trynd, Skill, Skill, Singed, Singed, Skill); the old chart scored level 6 for Tryndamere while its own spikes[1] and whys[4] both describe Singed winning it. NOT ASSERTED: the content layer says Mega Adhesive 'cuts off the Spinning Slash escape route', which is a grounding claim. Mega Adhesive does ground, but Riot's Spinning Slash text is 'slices toward a target unit' with no dash flag in the kit and no enemy-dash-deniable rule in _missing for this pair, so I left the existing sentence alone rather than sharpen or repeat it. Worth a human ruling — see questionsForUser.
